title: Prototype Pollution in 101 via set/put keypaths
longFix: `set` and `put` passed user-supplied keypaths directly to keypather, which walks `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` segments. All keypather writes now go through a guard that rejects keypaths targeting a prototype slot.
summary: The `set` and `put` functions accept a dotted/bracketed keypath and delegate to the `keypather` library to assign a nested value. A keypath such as `__proto__.polluted` or `constructor.prototype.polluted` causes keypather to walk into and mutate `Object.prototype`, affecting every object in the process. This is reachable from the 3-arg, 2-arg, and partial-application forms of both functions.
fixExplanation: A small `_safe-keypath.js` wrapper validates every keypath before it reaches keypather; keypaths whose segments resolve to `__proto__`, `constructor`, or `prototype` are rejected (the write is skipped). Legitimate keypaths — including keys that merely contain those words as substrings, e.g. `constructorName` — are unaffected.
